The problem with visual programming is that you lose too much time to develop it and they do not scale well.

Most people aren't interested in the fundamentals when they first start programming. Most people just want to accomplish something simple. Usually when people are attempting to learn programming they already have a project in mind, or an ultimate end goal. In my case, I wanted to know how I could make a video game. I think, if you are trying to encourage people to learn programming, you should go top-down not bottom-up as you are suggesting here. Start off with something like visual programming, or a high level language like Python or Ruby (with a helpful stack in place) and then give them the power to explore from there. Eventually they'll want to do something outside of the box, then you move them to an environment that gives them the space to accomplish those goals. Here is a great example of a tool for learning programming.

https://www.bloc.io/ruby-warrior/#/
